author: einrikr
text:
I had it all figured out on this one!

But as it turned out, I hadn't.

There was a FL confirmation. There was an engulf. Price went back up
nicely, via another QM (at green zone) but the R of that was really low.
 Price went to my UFL, went down and came back up to get the last set of
 orders there and went down again. Triggered my TP for partial profit,
bounced a bit lower and got back up again, to the FL above my UFL.
Played out different than I expected but happily, it didn't cost me
anything.

Price did everything I thought it'd do, except for reacting the way I predicted. I guess this is a nice exercise in scale.

Back to the drawing board!

text:
Thanks for the encouraging words IF! I think that trusting yourself is one of the hardest parts of this business...

In the light of "trusting your own readings", I held on to the long
trade I entered yesterday. According to my analysis, price could go
quite a bit higher before hitting my TG. Of course, there are several
TG's along the way but I'd like to see how far it goes. When I went to
bed yesterday, it was at around 20R. After my first cup of coffee this
morning, I checked and saw that it'd hit 51R and plummeted to a point
very close to my entry point. That is what I still find very scary.
Although I made profit on this trade already, I didn't want it to hit my
 SL.

Now, I did feel the urge to close the trade and take a bit of extra profit but I didn't. There were 2 reasons for that (see chart):

1: There's a nice cap to hold price up

2: Price went to QM level and got back up.

The trade is now back up at 26R already and I'm holding on to it until
price tells me to get out or it hits my TG. All in all, this really
helps in developing trust in my readings and especially, feeling
comfortable with the material taught here. Thank you for that IF and all
 fellow members of RTM. It's an honor to be part of such a community.

author: einrikr
text:
Hi Manouche,

What I came up with is this:

The pink dotted line is an RS-level, with good history. Price visited this region many times over the past.

What I learned from this missed trade is a few things:

- Always take spread into account

- When price hits MPL, it's bound to break it on subsequent returns.

So price was bound to break both my entry level (but not before it hit my TG) and my TG.

Looking into this a bit deeper (on higher timeframe, so to say), the
kink of my TG is quite a bit bigger and price hit the MPL of that, when
visiting my entry point again, It went a bit deeper down, and risen back
 up but the overall RR of that trade would be lower than the one I was
planning to take.

Hope it's of any help! Please do take into account that this is my take
on what happened and what I've learned from it, so it might not be
correct, strictly speaking.

author: einrikr
text:
After 3 days, I’ve closed my trade at 50R, be it by accident. Not the
most efficient trade but highly rewarding. Wanted to bank 50% but it
didn’t work, the action I performed close 100%.

However, what have I learned from this trade:

Targets

Setting a final TG for yourself is a good thing, so you know what you’re
 working up to. Watching it reaching your target helps building trust in
 your reads.

Do not however, neglect mid-range targets as they are very capable of
bouncing price. For example, price bounced off of 2 PCP points and got
as low as the cap of my point of entry.

It was a fun exercise though, getting in to a short, down to the PO I’ve
 set for a long and seeing price hit exactly that and turn around. There
 was 0.7 pip drawdown on this trade.

Expectations

50R (high of first day) or 70R (high of second day) is more than enough. Just be happy with it and take it.

I’ve been waiting for a bit higher R for 3 days now and it bugs me. It’s
 really annoying to see price going up and down and not hitting your TG.
 Sure, it didn’t hit my stop but the bit of extra R is not worth the
wait. Not for me it isn’t, not at this point in my trading career at
least. Maybe it’ll be later on. I’m not in a hurry, not in the need of
getting high R trades but the inconvenience of waiting and watching PA
all day long, sort of defeats the result for me. On the other hand, if
it turns out that I’m able to do this on regular bases, it gives me the
opportunity to do a lot of thing I like, rather than a day job. Future
goals, I guess ;-)

Patience is very important in this line of work but being satisfied with
 quite high R results is equally important. You have to be patient to
let price come up to the level you set as your TG and you have to have
faith in tour readings. You have to be realistic too, and not let your
final TG play with your mind.

All in all, this trade showed me the very basics, like caps working, CP,
 and some QM levels even. It has been good fun, watching price doing
it’s thing, at least for the first 2 days. Today, not so much for me but
 now I wanted to hold on to it and get the profit I predicted it to
give. It was a good experience, of which I’ve learned a lot. It works
wonders for me to witness price doing what it does at certain levels and
 I’m very happy with the result and especially of everything it taught
me.

On to the next! But I'm going to bed first, really tired after watching the screen for 3 days!

author: einrikr
text:
I'm having a not-so-wonderful trading week so far but that happens. I
decided to take the day off and do some manual labour and that was a
good thing.

Coming home, I decided to watch price a bit and marked up this, regarding the pinball nature of price:

(1) Price came, breaks QM level from the past so made LSK here. Currently holding price up.

(2) Price bounced from RSK in the past

(3) FTB of current FL. Important cap, that will hold price up until engulfed.

(4) Price hit PCP kink in the past. Still holding price down.

(5) Important cap (see 3) holds price up.

(6) FTB of newest LSK holding price down. Price goes to LFL.

(7) Price engulfs important cap (3) and gets back up.

( Price hits LTF QM level, price is now trapped between this lvl and the currently active LFL.

(9) Price hits MPL (i.e. QM Level) of LFL. Goes back up.

(10) Last LTF UFL engulfed

(11) Price comes down to last cap.

(12) Current UFL still active.

There are QM level bounces at 4, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 12. I actually think that 11 is a QM level bounce as well.

Now, I'm too tired to distill any more out of it at the moment but I
guess the main thing here is: price travels from QM to QM, in different
scales.

You can take a 1RR trade going from marker 7 to marker 8 for example, or
 take a 7RR trade from marker 9 to 12. I think this is all a matter of
scale, focus on the lower scales only, you get the lower R trades. Focus
 on larger scale ranges, combined with lower scale entry, and you're
getting the real high R trades.

Now, I haven't checked this on any other charts since the before made
statement of tiredness, but I'll keep diving in this matter the upcoming
 days. In the mean time, please feel free to comment. If I'm just
rambling nonsense, please just tell me too, so I won't focus on this any
 more
